clue.text: Container ship

definitions.meaning: a small parcel or carton that holds goods
a ... boat, a vessel carrying mail and passengers on a regular route

explanation.surface: A container ship, the kind that carries freight boxes across the oceans.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a parcel holding goods, and the old mail boat called a packet boat.

clue.text: Piped music

parts.note: reads like background music played in shops, but means music played on the bagpipes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Piped music' usually means recorded music in lifts and shops; here it is music for the Highland bagpipes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pibroch is a classical Scottish composition played on the bagpipes, so literally piped music.

clue.text: Alice is out to get her

indicators.note: being out means out of place or disordered, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alice has left the house, so someone else will have to fetch her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out' rearranges the letters of ALICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name stands for a woman, referred to by the pronoun in the clue.

clue.text: Discovering English work of intelligence

parts.note: espionage is the work of an intelligence service

explanation.surface: Uncovering the secrets of English intelligence operations.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, so the participle is a synonym of finding or spotting.

clue.text: Pose, holding award: a form of acceptance

indicators.note: one piece holds, or contains, the other within it

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose
the OBE is the Order of the British Empire, a British honour

explanation.surface: A celebrity poses with an award, graciously accepting it.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase expresses resigned acceptance, like saying very well then.

clue.text: Processed heroin available at a price

indicators.note: processing a raw material changes its form, so the letters of the word are reworked

explanation.surface: Refined heroin can be bought if you pay enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Processed' rearranges HEROIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something for rent can be had for a fee, which is what being available at a price means.

clue.text: Complicated to work out

definitions.meaning: to develop a plan in full detail

explanation.definitionFit: As adjective it means intricate; as a verb it means to develop or expand in detail.

clue.text: Forcibly puts forward awkward truths to school head

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy or ill-fitting, so the word's letters are disordered
the head of a word is its first letter, taken from the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone bluntly presses uncomfortable facts upon the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges TRUTHS into THRUST; the 'head' of 'school' gives S. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To shove or push something forward forcefully is the verb's sense here.

clue.text: Confirmed they do lie down all over the place

indicators.note: scattered in disarray, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some people lie down here, there and everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges THEY DO LIE DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone confirmed in their views is thoroughly committed, as wool dyed before weaving keeps its colour.

clue.text: Stygian fare

parts.note: looks like gloomy food, but means the fee for the ferry across the river Styx

explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth a coin was placed with the dead to pay Charon the ferryman over the Styx.
explanation.definitionFit: This small ancient Greek coin was the payment the dead gave the ferryman of the underworld.

clue.text: A subject for those who have a mind to study

definitions.text: A subject for those who have a mind to study

parts.words: A subject for those who have a mind to study
parts.note: 'have a mind to study' suggests keenness, but read literally it is studying the mind

explanation.walkthrough: 'have a mind to' means feel inclined to; read literally, the subject is the study of the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical speciality treats mental illness, so its students study the mind itself.

clue.text: Thus a West African country becomes an East African

parts.note: so means thus, in that way
Mali is a landlocked country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A geography puzzle in which a western nation turns into an eastern one.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Somalia, on the Horn of Africa, is a native of that eastern region.

clue.text: Party member who went to pot

definitions.text: Party member who went to pot

parts.words: Party member who went to pot
parts.note: sounds like a ruined politician, but means a guest at a tea party pushed into a teapot

explanation.walkthrough: In Alice in Wonderland the sleepy guest at the Mad Hatter's tea party is put into the teapot.
explanation.definitionFit: This small sleepy rodent attends the Mad Hatter's tea party and ends up stuffed in the teapot.

clue.text: Its members have strong links

parts.note: suggests a close-knit group, but the links are literal iron chains joining prisoners

explanation.walkthrough: Convicts were chained together to work outdoors, so the bond between them was literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of prisoners chained together while doing hard labour are joined by metal links.

clue.text: I'm ready with first-rate ad-lib

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
prompt means ready and quick to act
U means upper-class, and so superior or first-rate

explanation.surface: A performer says they are ready with a brilliant improvised line.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is an old British label for refined or superior usage. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An improvised remark or performance, made up on the spot, is an ad-lib.

clue.text: Deep sea fish

definitions.meaning: low in pitch, as a voice
a spiny-finned fish of the sea

explanation.surface: A fish that lives deep in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the lowest male voice, the other a common edible marine fish.

clue.text: EXCELS

parts.note: the word means outdoes, and it is also printed entirely in upper-case letters

explanation.walkthrough: The clue works twice: to outdo is to top, and the word is set in capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To top or outdo something is one sense; letters printed in upper case is the other.

clue.text: Arching in embarrassment

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new arrangement, in a state of upset that matches the surface

explanation.surface: Someone arches their back in embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' rearranges ARCHING; the setter leans on the surface image of an awkward squirm.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation or mortification at failure, a close synonym of embarrassment.

clue.text: Dare to raise objection

definitions.meaning: a dare is a provocation to prove oneself
to dispute or question a decision

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a call to prove oneself and the act of disputing a claim, as in court.

clue.text: Left one gainfully employed as an apprentice

parts.note: someone in paid work is a wage earner

explanation.surface: A worker who has quit, now in paid work as a trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee or apprentice is still a beginner learning the trade.

clue.text: Several flukes prevent the balloon going up

definitions.text: Several flukes prevent the balloon going up

parts.words: Several flukes prevent the balloon going up
parts.note: flukes look like lucky breaks, but are the pointed prongs of an anchor holding a balloon down

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flukes' are the barbed arms of an anchor; this small many-armed anchor was used to moor balloons.
explanation.definitionFit: A small anchor with several prongs, it can hook the ground and hold a balloon down.

clue.text: Cloth worker?

parts.note: suggests a weaver, but 'the cloth' is the clergy, so a worker in the church

explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' is a traditional name for the clergy, from clerical dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman belongs to the profession known as the cloth.

clue.text: Holy orders?

parts.note: usually means ordination as a priest, but read here as commands issued by the church

explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy orders' normally means the rank of clergy; the question mark asks for the church's rules instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Church law is literally the set of holy commands, the body of rules made by church authority.

clue.text: Jack has a way with him in foreign parts

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
a road is a way

explanation.surface: A sailor with a knack for getting by in other countries.
explanation.walkthrough: AB (able-bodied seaman) and Jack both mean sailor. 'has a' and 'with him' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overseas is to be in foreign parts.

clue.text: Show, we hear, to look back on

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard spoken, so its sound gives the letters

parts.note: to review the past is to look back on it

explanation.surface: A performance, apparently, that one can look back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical entertainment of sketches and songs is a kind of show.

clue.text: One needs capital, becoming number one in France

parts.note: becoming means fitting or seemly, as proper does
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A businessman needs money to become France's leading figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning fitting. 'One needs capital' means needs a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A name for a particular person or place must be written with a capital initial letter.

clue.text: It turns to face the blow

definitions.text: It turns to face the blow

parts.words: It turns to face the blow
parts.note: sounds like someone bracing for a punch, but the blow is the wind

explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' is the wind; a weathercock swings round to point into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather indicator on a roof swings round so it points into the wind.

clue.text: Aunt about to get a distinction in Indian dance

indicators.note: about means around or astir, so the letters are turned around

parts.note: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British honour

explanation.surface: An aunt wins an award for Indian dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges AUNT into NAUT. 'to get' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional dance performed by professional dancing girls in India.

clue.text: Trial to find alternative to softwood

parts.note: the word or introduces an alternative
deal is fir or pine timber

explanation.surface: A test to find something other than softwood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful experience that tests endurance is a trial.
